content: A hair whorl is a localized area of hair that grows in a direction opposite to the surrounding hair. This phenomenon is observed in most hairy animals. Hair whorls can be found on various parts of the body, including the head. Specifically, hair whorls located on the head, known as parietal whorls, have been extensively studied due to their suggested association with brain development and abnormal hair whorl patterns. This connection is thought to arise because both brain cells and skin cells originate from the ectodermal tissue of the embryo. Abnormal hair whorls are often used as an early indicator of atypical temperament in many domesticated animals, particularly in cattle. They are also utilized in assessing the mental status of primates, including humans. Normal parietal whorls on the scalp typically present as either a single whorl or double whorls. While triple parietal scalp whorls are less common, their presence does not necessarily signify any abnormality. The absence of hair whorls entirely or the presence of whorls in abnormal locations on the scalp is generally considered a potential marker of abnormal brain development.
